extracted.subtask_description: News coverage and public response around allegations of fabricated stories by a comedian, including journalistic standards and the comedian's rebuttal. Focuses on fact-checking, corroboration, context, and audience accountability in celebrity reporting and comedic storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful reporting and fact‑checking
rubrics_metrics.description: "This piece was carefully reported and fact-checked"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The New Yorker statement emphasizes rigorous reporting and fact-checking as a standard; the article notes the profile was "based on interviews with more than twenty people," implying breadth of reporting and verification (former staffers, security team, subjects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple independent sources for corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters should corroborate claims by interviewing many relevant people and documenting sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The profile is described as relying on interviews with "more than twenty people," including former staffers, members of the subject's security team, and people featured in the subject's standup, indicating a standard of multiple, varied corroborating sources for contested factual claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context and corroborating materials when responding
rubrics_metrics.description: When disputed, the subject should provide context and materials to corroborate their accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hasan says he provided the magazine "further details and materials to corroborate his stories," and in his response he played audio and showed excerpts of emails/exchanges to support his version; the article frames provision of such evidence as a way to address allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about omissions and factual errors
rubrics_metrics.description: "There were omissions and factual errors in The New Yorker article that misrepresented my life story," — openness about what was omitted or incorrect is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comedian framed his video as giving "full transparency," supplying the omitted context and materials. This suggests a standard that parties should explicitly identify and correct omissions or factual mistakes when challenging coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish standards across comedic formats (facts vs emotions)
rubrics_metrics.description: "In political comedy, facts come first. In comedic storytelling, emotions come first."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page relays Minhaj's asserted distinction: political/news-oriented comedy requires rigorous fact-checking, whereas storytelling/comedic performance may prioritize emotional truth and artistic choices. This functions as a criterion for evaluating truthfulness depending on comedic genre and platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge embellishment and accept accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: If artistic embellishment was used, acknowledge it and apologize to those harmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hasan "apologized to fans who felt hurt by the story" and "explained instances where he embellished or changed details." The article treats apology and admission of embellishment as part of responsible response when stories cause harm or betrayal of trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect subjects' identity and guard against doxing/harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Protecting individuals featured in anecdotes is a responsibility; avoid exposing identities that could lead to doxing or threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hasan claimed he "continually did all he could to protect Bethany’s identity," showing emails where she thanked him; the New Yorker reported the woman had been a victim of doxing and death threats — highlighting the importance of identity protection and assessing whether reporting or storytelling exposed subjects to harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize specific factual details (timing and sequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide accurate specifics about timing and sequence of events to avoid misleading impressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Minhaj explained the prom conversation "took place a few days before prom," not on the prom night as might have been implied — demonstrating the importance of precise contextual details when recounting anecdotes.
